newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-EAGLES COME BACK TO EDGE JETS AND AVOID EMBARRASSING DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-EAGLES COME BACK TO EDGE JETS AND AVOID EMBARRASSING DEFEAT.

text.p: Eagles quarterback Ty Detmer avoided having to don a dunce cap by throwing three second-half TD passes to rally Philadelphia from a 13-point deficit to a 21-20 win over the New York Jets.

A slip of the tongue by Detmer earlier in the week spurred on the NFL-worst Jets (1-14). The quarterback called playing the Jets a no-win situation and that his team would look like the "biggest idiots in the world" with a defeat.

The Eagles trailed throughout and avoided an embarrassing defeat when Detmer connected for a touchdown pass to Irving Fryar with 5:29 left. Philadelphia (9-6) can clinch a playoff berth if Washington loses at Arizona on Sunday.
"We won ugly, but we won," said Fryar, who caught two touchdown passes. "They played hard the whole game, not like a team with a losing record that wanted to go home."
Said Detmer: "They played with a lot of pride. They made it a dog fight."
Detmer's go-ahead touchdown pass followed the second interception of the game by safety Mike Zordich that gave Philadelphia possession at the Jets 18. Fryar caught four passes for 92 yards.
Detmer, who completed 17-of-34 passes for 198 yards, threw a two-yard touchdown pass to Chris T. Jones one minute 35 seconds earlier.
"We had to find a way to win the football game," Eagles coach Ray Rhodes said. "It was important for us to come up with plays to make things happen."
It was yet another bitter defeat for embattled Jets head coach Rich Kotite, who was fired by the Eagles after losing his final seven games of the 1994 season.
Kotite has lost 27 of his 31 games as head coach of the Jets, who fell to a franchise-worst 1-14 this season.
"We made some big plays but it still wasn't enough," Kotite said. "We were pathetic on offence. We turned the ball over five times and we couldn't run the ball."
Jets defensive end Hugh Douglas, who had threatened to hurt Detmer if he got his hands on him, played an inspired game with three sacks and a fumble recovery.
The game featured nine turnovers, including four interceptions of Jets quarterback Glenn Foley, who completed 16-of-26 passes for 186 yards. On the ground, New York had just 53 yards on 23 carries.
A 46-yard flea flicker touchdown pass from Foley to Keyshawn Johnson accounted for the first score of the game late in the first quarter.
The extra point gave Jets' kicker Nick Lowery 1,700 career points, moving him past Jan Stenured into second on the all-time scoring list behind George Blanda.
The Jets made it 10-0 on a 27-yard field goal by Lowery with 4:22 left in the second quarter.
Philadelphia cut the lead to three points on a 40-yard touchdown pass from Detmer to Fryar midway through the second quarter. An interception by Zordich set up the score.
The Jets pushed their lead to 17-7 when Glenn stepped in front of a pass for Fryar and went 13 yards to the end zone.
Lowery hit another field goal with two seconds left in the third quarter to make it 20-7 before Detmer led the comeback.
In Chicago, Dave Krieg threw for 217 yards and three touchdowns as the Chicago Bears dealt a severe blow to the San Diego Chargers' playoff hopes with a 27-14 victory.
Krieg, who completed 24-of-37 passes, threw a pair seven-yard touchdowns and an eight-yard score for the Bears (7-8), who already had been eliminated from playoff contention.
San Diego (7-8) will be shut out of the playoffs should Indianapolis win at Kansas City on Sunday.

Chargers quarterback Stan Humphries returned after suffering a concussion in a 45-7 loss to New England two weeks ago. He got San Diego on the board fast with 20-yard touchdown pass to Andre Coleman just 2:22 into the game.
Jeff Jaeger's 45-yard field goal broke a 14-14 tie with 6:05 remaining in the third period. Jaeger later added a 40-yarder for the Bears with 1:04 to go.
